places.label: Pripyat Marshes
places.body: The Pripyat wetlands of Polesia form part of the broad reconstructed ancestral region. Settlement dots favour raised margins, sandy terraces and neighbouring river valleys rather than uniformly filling the bog. This label does not assert one exact homeland or a known medieval resource map.

events.label: Zarubintsy cultural horizon
events.body: Archaeological precursor context. A cultural horizon is not a bounded linguistic or genetic population; no extra migrant cohort is created.

events.label: Wielbark cultural horizon
events.body: Gothic-associated regional context retained from the report. This is not a Slavic migrant cohort or an exact dated Scandinavian departure.

events.label: Kyiv culture and ancestral staging
events.body: Broad ancestral proxy in the Dnieper region. Exact homeland boundaries and contemporaneous reference genomes remain unresolved.

events.label: Sorabi recorded on the Elbe
events.body: Frankish annals record the Sorabi on the Elbe in 806 CE. This is a textual attestation, not the date their settlement began.

events.label: Moravian Slavs in Frankish annals
events.body: The supplied report cites Sclavos Marganses under 846 CE. This recorded presence is distinct from the earlier reconstructed settlement interval.

events.label: Branimir and Dalmatian inscriptions
events.body: The report discusses church inscriptions naming Branimir and varying Slavic/Croat titles. These concern regional identity and rulership, not an additional census or a single arrival.

events.label: Pottery technology spreads in settled communities
events.body: Feldberg, Tornow and Leipzig wares represent technology transfer and political consolidation in this reconstruction. No new migration population is attached to this event.
